account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: market business, town accounts, tea with neighbour at the dockside cottage, and afternoon office business. A few things suggest people may be arranging something without keeping me fully informed. Neighbour mentioned the bakery lights, saying the baker called them everyday cheer, but gave no definite news about gatherings or dock changes. The baker had stocked thirty-two loaves and asked whether any town gatherings would need bread. Later I noticed freight carrying bread through the town hall, apparently into the great hall, with an emerald in hand. I have asked the secretary whether refreshments are being arranged, but have not received an answer to that question.

The clearest development is the innkeeper's request, relayed by the secretary, for a civic presentation thanking me for public service tomorrow from 18:00 to 18:30 in the great hall. Hospitality workers and tradespeople are involved, according to the secretary. They specifically want me to arrive no earlier than 18:00 because preparations will last until then. I already approved this, though the secretary has just asked for approval again. My best guess is that the bread and perhaps the other small hints relate to preparations for that presentation, possibly a surprise celebration. That connection is not confirmed; bakery lights and ordinary bread deliveries could be unrelated. I have no evidence of wrongdoing. The treasury contained 128 emeralds, and the secretary reported no unusual expenses or funding requests, although we did not locate account records to verify the accounts.
